To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Drosophila visual transduction is mediated, at least in part, by lipid second messengers, rather than by IP3; 2) DAG is the likely candidate; 3) PUFAs are also likely to be involved in the activation of Drosophlia TRP channels; and 4) the reduction of PIP2 may also contribute to the activation of TRP channel.

Drosophila trp and trpl genes are required for light adaptation and phototransduction in photoreceptors, and that their regulation is mediated, not only by IP3, but also by other lipid messengers, such as DAG, its metabolites, PUFAs, and PIP2.
TRP channels in Drosophilaphotoreceptors are regulated by lipid messengers and that this is likely to be a general mechanism for activation of this family of ion channels.

understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the activation of TRP channel by lipid messengers, which is a fundamental problem in the biology of TRP channels and in the biology of vision.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate Drosophila visual transduction, and how they are related to human disease.
the molecular basis of TRP channel activation by lipids and the role of these channels in the transduction of sensory signals in the nervous system.
